features.feature_value: Remove when the post resorts to name-calling/attacks; allow only if it reads as productive, non-hateful discussion
features.evidence_span: "If it looked like the posts resorted to name calling or attacks/name calling I tended to remove them."
features.rationale: They explicitly describe a linguistic/behavioral rule linking attacks/name-calling to removal.

features.feature_value: Remove items felt to be encroaching on hate speech even while trying to stay politically neutral
features.evidence_span: "I tried to stay neutral politically but opted to remove things I felt were encroaching on hate speech."
features.rationale: They state neutrality plus a specific threshold related to hate-speech encroachment.

features.feature_value: Vulgar language causes immediate rejection; also consider how probing statements are for further discussion/opinion
features.evidence_span: "If the statement contained vulgar language, they were immediately rejected."
features.rationale: They provide a clear decision trigger (vulgar language → immediate rejection).

features.feature_value: Remove if there are slurs or defamatory statements about someone’s character
features.evidence_span: "if there was any slurs, or defamatory on ones character"
features.rationale: They name slurs and defamation as direct grounds affecting the decision.

features.feature_value: Lack of prior knowledge led to voting not to allow; also driven by being horrified by the rhetoric type
features.evidence_span: "I was overall horrified by the type of rhetoric in the posts."
features.rationale: They tie emotional reaction (horrified) and limited familiarity to their keep/remove choices.

features.feature_value: Compare two different views and assess the attitude behind them
features.evidence_span: "I tried to look through 2 different views. And to look at the attitude behind it."
features.rationale: Their method focuses on comparing both perspectives and interpreting underlying attitude.

features.feature_value: Decisions depend on whether the pair refers to the same event or different events that could be viewed negatively by the opposing party
features.evidence_span: "If they were the same event or different events that could’ve been viewed in the same negative light by the opposing party"
features.rationale: They describe an event-level comparison criterion grounded in opposing-party perception.

features.feature_value: Decision depends on whether the content targets general populations vs individual people
features.evidence_span: "If they were attaching general populations or if they were attacking individual people."
features.rationale: They specify a content-targeting distinction (group vs individual) as influencing the decision.
